title: Arakhin 6
description: When may the Temple accept a gentile’s gift, what becomes of a gentile’s teruma or a beam with God’s name on it, may one use a sela pledged to charity, may a synagogue’s donated lamp be put to other use, and why one taken to be executed is neither vowed nor valuated.
topics: 🏛️ Gifts of gentiles to the Temple: refused at the beginning of the building, at the end only if not a defined item
📜 Nehemiah’s letter to Asaph: a government does not retract
🌾 A gentile’s teruma and a beam with God’s name: perhaps his heart was toward Heaven
🪙 “This sela is for charity”: may he use it, for himself or for another, and what about “upon me”?
🕎 A lamp donated to a synagogue: Sha’azrak the Arab and the anger in Pumbedita
⚖️ The moribund and one taken to be executed: neither vowed nor valuated, says the mishna; Rabbi Ḥanina ben Akavya and Rabbi Yosei
🚫 “Anything dedicated of men shall not be redeemed”: no ransom for a death sentence of the court
💸 If he caused damage: Rav Yosef and Rava on loans by oral agreement and loans written in the Torah

a1.he: תָּנָא חֲדָא: גּוֹי שֶׁהִתְנַדֵּב נְדָבָה לְבֶדֶק הַבַּיִת מְקַבְּלִים הֵימֶנּוּ, וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ: אֵין מְקַבְּלִין!

a2.he: אָמַר רַבִּי אִילָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא — בַּתְּחִילָּה, הָא — בַּסּוֹף.

a3.he: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בִּתְחִילָּה, אֲפִילּוּ מַיִם וּמֶלַח אֵין מְקַבְּלִין מֵהֶם. בַּסּוֹף, דָּבָר הַמְסוּיָּים אֵין מְקַבְּלִין, דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְסוּיָּים מְקַבְּלִין. הֵיכִי דָּמֵי דָּבָר הַמְסוּיָּים? אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: כְּגוֹן אַמָּה כָּלְיָא עוֹרֵב.

a4.he: מֵתִיב רַב יוֹסֵף: ״וְאִיגֶּרֶת אֶל אָסָף שׁוֹמֵר הַפַּרְדֵּס אֲשֶׁר לַמֶּלֶךְ וְגוֹ׳״. אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבַּיֵּי: שָׁאנֵי מַלְכוּתָא דְּלָא הָדְרָא בַּיהּ, דְּאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: אִי אָמַר מַלְכוּתָא ״עָקַרְנָא טוּרֵי״, עָקַר טוּרֵי וְלָא הָדַר בֵּיהּ.

a5.he: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: גּוֹי שֶׁהִפְרִישׁ תְּרוּמָה מִכִּרְיוֹ, בּוֹדְקִין אוֹתוֹ, אִי בְּדַעַת יִשְׂרָאֵל הִפְרִישָׁהּ — תִּינָּתֵן לַכֹּהֵן, וְאִם לָאו — טְעוּנָה גְּנִיזָה, חָיְישִׁינַן שֶׁמָּא בְּלִבּוֹ לַשָּׁמַיִם.

a6.he: מֵיתִיבִי: גּוֹי שֶׁהִתְנַדֵּב קוֹרָה, וְשֵׁם כָּתוּב עָלֶיהָ — בּוֹדְקִין אוֹתוֹ, אִם אָמַר: ״בְּדַעַת יִשְׂרָאֵל הִפְרַשְׁתִּיהָ״ — יָגוֹד וְיִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בַּמּוֹתָר, וְאִם לָאו — טְעוּנָה גְּנִיזָה, חָיְישִׁינַן שֶׁמָּא בְּלִבּוֹ לַשָּׁמַיִם.

a7.he: טַעְמָא דְּשֵׁם כָּתוּב עָלֶיהָ, דְּבָעֲיָא גְּנִיזָה; הָא אֵין שֵׁם כָּתוּב עָלֶיהָ — לָא בָּעֲיָא גְּנִיזָה!

a8.he: הוּא הַדִּין דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּאֵין שֵׁם כָּתוּב עָלֶיהָ נָמֵי בָּעֲיָא גְּנִיזָה, וְהָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן, דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּשֵׁם כָּתוּב עָלֶיהָ, יָגוֹד וְיִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בַּמּוֹתָר, דְּשֵׁם שֶׁלֹּא בִּמְקוֹמוֹ לָאו קָדוֹשׁ.

a9.he: דִּתְנַן: הָיָה כָּתוּב עַל יְדוֹת הַכֵּלִים וְעַל כַּרְעֵי הַמִּטָּה — הֲרֵי זֶה יָגוֹד וְיִגְנוֹז.

a10.he: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבָהוּ: הָאוֹמֵר ״סֶלַע זוֹ לִצְדָקָה״ — מוּתָּר לְשַׁנּוֹתָהּ. סְבוּר מִינַּהּ: לְעַצְמוֹ — אִין, לְאַחֵר — לָא. אִיתְּמַר: אָמַר רַב אַמֵּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בֵּין לְעַצְמוֹ בֵּין לְאַחֵר.

a11.he: אָמַר רַבִּי זְעֵירָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא דְּאָמַר ״עָלַי״, אֲבָל אָמַר ״הֲרֵי זוֹ״ — בְּעֵינַאּ בָּעֵי לְמִיתְּבַהּ.

a12.he: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רָבָא: אַדְּרַבָּה, אִיפְּכָא מִיסְתַּבְּרָא — אָמַר ״זוֹ״ מִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בָּהּ, כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלִיחַיַּיב בְּאַחְרָיוּתַהּ, אֲבָל אָמַר ״עָלַי״ — לָא! אֶלָּא, לָא שְׁנָא.

a13.he: תַּנְיָא כְּוָותֵיהּ דְּרָבָא: נֶדֶר צְדָקָה, וְאֵין הֶקְדֵּשׁ צְדָקָה. מַאי קָאָמַר? לָא נֶדֶר וְלָא הֶקְדֵּשׁ צְדָקָה!

a14.he: אֶלָּא לָאו הָכִי קָאָמַר: צְדָקָה הֲרֵי הִיא בְּבַל תְּאַחֵר, וְאֵינָהּ כְּהֶקְדֵּשׁ, דְּאִילּוּ הֶקְדֵּשׁ אֲסִיר לְאִשְׁתַּמּוֹשֵׁי בֵּיהּ, וְאִילּוּ צְדָקָה שְׁרֵי לְאִשְׁתַּמּוֹשֵׁי בֵּיהּ.

a15.he: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: אַמְרִיתָא לִשְׁמַעְתָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב זְבִיד מִנְּהַרְדְּעָא, אָמַר: אַתּוּן הָכִי מַתְנִיתוּ לַהּ, אֲנַן הָכִי מַתְנֵינַן לַהּ — אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ אָמַר רַב: הָאוֹמֵר ״סֶלַע זוֹ לִצְדָקָה״ מוּתָּר לְשַׁנּוֹתָהּ, בֵּין לְעַצְמוֹ בֵּין לְאַחֵר, בֵּין אָמַר ״עָלַי״ בֵּין אָמַר ״הֲרֵי זוֹ״.

a16.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״סֶלַע זוֹ לִצְדָקָה״ — עַד שֶׁלֹּא בָּאתָה לְיַד גַּבַּאי, מוּתָּר לְשַׁנּוֹתָהּ; מִשֶּׁבָּאתָה לְיַד גַּבַּאי, אָסוּר לְשַׁנּוֹתָהּ.

b1.he: אִינִי? וְהָא רַבִּי יַנַּאי יָזֵיף וּפָרַע! שָׁאנֵי רַבִּי יַנַּאי, דְּנִיחָא לְהוּ לַעֲנִיִּים דְּכַמָּה דִּמְשַׁהֵי מְעַשֵּׂה וּמַיְיתֵי לְהוּ.

b2.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהִתְנַדֵּב מְנוֹרָה אוֹ נֵר לְבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת — אָסוּר לְשַׁנּוֹתָהּ. סָבַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא לְמֵימָר: לָא שְׁנָא לִדְבַר הָרְשׁוּת וְלָא שְׁנָא לִדְבַר מִצְוָה. אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַמֵּי: הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן — לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא לִדְבַר הָרְשׁוּת, אֲבָל לִדְבַר מִצְוָה מוּתָּר לְשַׁנּוֹתָהּ.

b3.he: מִדְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: גּוֹי שֶׁהִתְנַדֵּב מְנוֹרָה אוֹ נֵר לְבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת, עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִשְׁתַּקַּע שֵׁם בְּעָלֶיהָ — אָסוּר לְשַׁנּוֹתָהּ, מִשֶּׁנִּשְׁתַּקַּע שֵׁם בְּעָלֶיהָ — מוּתָּר לְשַׁנּוֹתָהּ.

b4.he: לְמַאי? אִילֵימָא לִדְבַר הָרְשׁוּת, מַאי אִירְיָא גּוֹי? אֲפִילּוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל נָמֵי!

b5.he: אֶלָּא לִדְבַר מִצְוָה, וְטַעְמָא דְּגוֹי הוּא דְּפָעֵי, אֲבָל יִשְׂרָאֵל דְּלָא פָּעֵי — שַׁפִּיר דָּמֵי.

b6.he: שַׁעַזְרַק טַיָּיעָא אִינַּדַּב שְׁרָגָא לְבֵי כְנִישְׁתָּא דְּרַב יְהוּדָה, שַׁנְּיֵיהּ רַחֲבָא וְאִיקְּפֵד רָבָא. אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: שַׁנְּיֵיהּ רָבָא וְאִיקְּפֵד רַחֲבָא, וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: שַׁנְּיֻיהּ חַזָּנֵי דְּפוּמְבְּדִיתָא, וְאִיקְּפֵד רַחֲבָא וְאִיקְּפֵד רַבָּה.

b7.he: מַאן דְּשַׁנְּיֵיהּ סָבַר דְּלָא שְׁכִיחַ, וּמַאן דְּאִיקְּפֵד סָבַר זִמְנִין דְּמִקְּרֵי וְאָתֵי.

b8.he: מַתְנִי׳ הַגּוֹסֵס וְהַיּוֹצֵא לֵיהָרֵג — לֹא נִידָּר וְלֹא נֶעֱרָךְ. רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן עֲקַבְיָא אוֹמֵר: נֶעֱרָךְ, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁדָּמָיו קְצוּבִין. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: נוֹדֵר וּמַעֲרִיךְ וּמַקְדִּישׁ, וְאִם הִזִּיק — חַיָּיב.

b9.he: גְּמָ׳ בִּשְׁלָמָא גּוֹסֵס לֹא נִידָּר — דְּלָאו בַּר דָּמִים הוּא, וְלֹא נֶעֱרָךְ — דְּלָאו בַּר הַעֲמָדָה וְהַעֲרָכָה הוּא, אֶלָּא יוֹצֵא לֵיהָרֵג, בִּשְׁלָמָא לֹא נִידָּר — דְּלָאו בַּר דָּמִים הוּא, אֶלָּא לֹא נֶעֱרָךְ אַמַּאי לָא?

b10.he: דְּתַנְיָא: מִנַּיִן הַיּוֹצֵא לֵיהָרֵג וְאָמַר ״עֶרְכִּי עָלַי״, שֶׁלֹּא אָמַר כְּלוּם? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״כׇּל חֵרֶם לֹא יִפָּדֶה״. יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ קוֹדֶם שֶׁנִּגְמַר דִּינוֹ? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״מִן הָאָדָם״, וְלֹא כׇּל הָאָדָם.

b11.he: וּלְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן עֲקַבְיָא, דְּאָמַר נֶעֱרָךְ מִפְּנֵי שֶׁדָּמָיו קְצוּבִין, הַאי ״כׇּל חֵרֶם״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ?

b12.he: לְכִדְתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר: לְפִי שֶׁמָּצִינוּ לַמּוּמָתִים בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם שֶׁנּוֹתְנִין מָמוֹן וּמִתְכַּפֵּר לָהֶם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״אִם כֹּפֶר יוּשַׁת עָלָיו״, יָכוֹל אַף בִּידֵי אָדָם כֵּן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״כׇּל חֵרֶם לֹא יִפָּדֶה״.

b13.he: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא מִיתוֹת חֲמוּרוֹת, שֶׁלֹּא נִיתְּנָה שִׁגְגָתָן לְכַפָּרָה, מִיתוֹת קַלּוֹת, שֶׁנִּיתְּנָה שִׁגְגָתָן לְכַפָּרָה, מִנַּיִן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״כׇּל חֵרֶם״.

b14.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: נוֹדֵר וּמַעֲרִיךְ כּוּ׳. וְתַנָּא קַמָּא מִי קָאָמַר דְּלָא?

b15.he: אֶלָּא, בְּנוֹדֵר וּמַעֲרִיךְ וּמִקַּדִּישׁ — כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי, כִּי פְלִיגִי — בְּאִם הִזִּיק. תַּנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר: אִם הִזִּיק — אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב בְּתַשְׁלוּמִין, וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי סָבַר: אִם הִזִּיק — חַיָּיב בְּתַשְׁלוּמִין.

b16.he: בְּמַאי קָמִיפַּלְגִי? אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: בְּמִלְוָה עַל פֶּה גּוֹבֶה מִן הַיּוֹרְשִׁין קָמִיפַּלְגִי, תַּנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר: מִלְוָה עַל פֶּה אֵינוֹ גּוֹבֶה מִן הַיּוֹרְשִׁין, וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי סָבַר: מִלְוָה עַל פֶּה גּוֹבֶה מִן הַיּוֹרְשִׁין.

b17.he: רָבָא אָמַר: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא מִלְוָה עַל פֶּה אֵינוֹ גּוֹבֶה מִן הַיּוֹרְשִׁין, וְהָכָא בְּמִלְוָה כְּתוּבָה בַּתּוֹרָה קָמִיפַּלְגִי, תַּנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר: מִלְוָה כְּתוּבָה בַּתּוֹרָה לָאו כִּכְתוּבָה בִּשְׁטָר דָּמְיָא, וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי סָבַר: כִּכְתוּבָה בִּשְׁטָר דָּמְיָא.

b18.he: וְאִיכָּא דְּמַתְנֵי לַהּ אַהָא: הַיּוֹצֵא לֵיהָרֵג, הוּא שֶׁחָבַל בַּאֲחֵרִים — חַיָּיב, אֲחֵרִים שֶׁחָבְלוּ בּוֹ — פְּטוּרִין. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: אַף הוּא אִם חָבַל בַּאֲחֵרִים — פָּטוּר, שֶׁלֹּא נִיתַּן לַחֲזָרַת עֲמִידַת בֵּית דִּין.

messages.text: 6a

Continued from 5b: Rava explained that the Jews of the Second Temple turned away the gentiles’ help (“You have nothing to do with us”) not for a halakhic reason but because the gentiles sought to weaken the hands of the builders.
§ The Gemara notes that there is an apparent contradiction with regard to the issue of whether or not a gentile may donate for the purpose of Temple maintenance. It was taught in one baraita:
In the case of a gentile who pledged a gift for Temple maintenance, one accepts it from him.

notes.dh: תני חדא עובד כוכבים שהתנדב לבדק הבית
notes.he: והא דלא מוקי לה כתנאי דר' יהודה ור' מאיר וכגון דליכא רפיון ידים כגון מן המלך דאם כן לא הו"ל למימר מקבלין ואין מקבלין אלא קדושה ואינה קדושה מבעיא ליה:
notes.en: It was taught in one baraita: a gentile who pledged a gift for Temple maintenance: The reason he does not establish [the two baraitot] as [a dispute of] tanna’im, Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Meir [above, 5b], in a case where there is no weakening of hands, such as [a gift] from the king, is that if so, he should not have said “one accepts” and “one does not accept”; rather, he would need [to say] “it is sanctified” and “it is not sanctified.”

messages.text: One does not accept it from him.

notes.dh: תני חדא עובד כוכבים שהתנדב לבדק הבית אין מקבלין ממנו כו'
notes.he: וא"ת ולישני הא ר' מאיר הא ר' יהודה וי"ל דא"כ קדושה ואינה קדושה מיבעיא ליה דאין מקבלין הימנו לבדק הבית [משמע דקדושה היא] ומשמע דתרוייהו סברי כר' יהודה:
notes.en: It was taught in one baraita: a gentile who pledged a gift for Temple maintenance, one does not accept from him, etc.: And if you say: let him answer that this is Rabbi Meir and that is Rabbi Yehuda; one can say that if so, he would need [to say] “it is sanctified” and “it is not sanctified.” [Saying] one does not accept it from him for Temple maintenance implies that it is sanctified, and it implies that both [baraitot] hold like Rabbi Yehuda.

messages.text: It is not difficult. This baraita, which teaches that the donation is not accepted, is stated with regard to the beginning of the building of the Temple. The donation is refused in order that the Jews not rely upon on the donations of gentiles. That baraita, which states that the donation is accepted, is stated with regard to the end of the building of the Temple, i.e., after it is already built.

notes.he: רש"י פי' לכתחילה שייך רפיון ידים ולבסוף לא שייך רפיון ידים ועוד פירש רבינו לכתחילה בתחילת הבנין יש לחוש פן יחזרו בהם ויערערו לומר יש לנו חלק בבית המקדש לבסוף דבר מסויים אין מקבלין פן יהיו לשם ולתפארת דבר שאין מסויים מקבלין דלא שייך תו ערעור הואיל ונבנה ב"ה כבר וניחא בזה הא דקאמר בסמוך שאני מלכותא דלא הדרא וליכא למיחש לעירעור:
notes.en: This at the beginning, that at the end: Rashi explained: at the beginning, weakening of hands applies, and at the end, weakening of hands does not apply. And our teacher further explained: at the beginning, at the start of the building, there is reason to fear that they might later go back and contest, saying: We have a share in the Temple. At the end, a defined item is not accepted, lest it serve them for a name and for glory; an item that is not defined is accepted, since contesting no longer applies once the Temple has already been built. This also explains well what is said shortly: the government is different, since it does not retract, and there is no fear of contesting.

notes.he: שאם אמר בתחלה רוצה אני להתנדב אמרי' לו שאין אנו מקבלין אותה אבל אם התנדב מקבלין אותה והיינו בסוף:
notes.en: This at the beginning, that at the end: if at the beginning he said: I wish to donate, we tell him that we do not accept it; but if he [already] donated, we accept it, and that is “at the end.”

messages.text: With regard to the beginning of the building of the Temple, one may not accept even water and salt from them.
messages.lead: As Rabbi Asi says that Rabbi Yoḥanan says with regard to donations of gentiles for Temple maintenance:

notes.he: בתחילת הבנין אין מקבלין דשמא לרפיון ידים מתכוונין:
notes.en: At the beginning: at the beginning of the building one does not accept, since perhaps they intend to weaken [the builders’] hands.

notes.he: דודאי למכירה עומד ולא יהא נראה בבנין אפי' הכי אין מקבלין:
notes.en: Even water and salt: which are certainly meant for sale and will not be visible in the building; even so, one does not accept.

messages.text: With regard to the end of the building of the Temple, one may not accept a defined item, i.e., if it will be clear that this was donated by a gentile. But one may accept their gift of an item that is not defined.

notes.he: לחזק את בדק דאין לומר רפיון ידים מקבלין. ל"א בתחילה כשלא היתה אימתן של עובדי כוכבים עליהן אין מקבלין אבל לבסוף מקבלין משום אימה. וראשון עיקר וזה אינו טעם דהא כל ימי בית שני היתה אימת העובדי כוכבים עליהן ובתחילתו יותר מסופו. וא"ת האי בתחילה נמי אמקדש ראשון קאמר א"כ מאי מותיב ליה לקמן מואגרת אל אסף וגו' דהיינו במקדש שני:
notes.en: At the end: [a gift] to strengthen the Temple’s upkeep, where one cannot say [they intend] weakening of hands, is accepted. Another version: at the beginning, when the fear of the gentiles was not upon them, one does not accept; but at the end one accepts, out of fear. The first [explanation] is the main one, and this [second] is no reason, since all the days of the Second Temple the fear of the gentiles was upon them, and at its beginning more than at its end. And if you say that this “at the beginning” refers to the First Temple too: if so, what is the objection raised below from “And a letter to Asaph,” etc., which concerns the Second Temple?

notes.he: שנראה בעין אין מקבלין מהם דגנאי הוא ועוד שמתפארים בו:
notes.en: A defined item: one that is visible to the eye. One does not accept it from them, since it is a disgrace, and moreover they boast of it.

notes.he: שהוא נראה בבנין אין מקבלין [מהם] משום לא לכם ולנו ועוד שמא יתחרט בו במה שנדר וירצה שיחזירוהו לו. אבל דבר שאינו מסויים ועומד למכירה מקבלין מהן. והאי דאמר אמה כלי עורב כלומר הא וכל דכותיה דהוי דבר הנראה:
notes.en: A defined item: one that is visible in the building is not accepted [from them], because of “not for you and for us” [to build; Ezra 4:3]; and moreover, lest he regret what he vowed and want it returned to him. But an item that is not defined and is meant for sale is accepted from them. And this “cubit kalya orev” means: this and anything like it that is a visible item.

messages.text: What is considered to be a defined item?
messages.quote: one may not accept a defined item

messages.text: For example, the cubit-wide spiked plates placed on the roof of the Sanctuary, which were designed to eliminate the ravens.
messages.quote: What is considered to be a defined item?

notes.he: להכי נקט אמה דאמרי' בפרק בתרא דמנחות (דף קז.) הרי עלי ברזל לא יפחות מאמה על אמה לכליא עורב שהיו מביאין טבלאות של ברזל אמה על אמה ובהן מסמרות גבוהין אמה קבועין ומחפין בהן ראש הגג של היכל לגרש את העורבים שלא ישכנו שם. כליא לשון שמגרש את העורבין כמו כייל דידבי כייל פרוחי דאמר במסכת נדה (דף יז. ע"ש) שהיה מגרש זבובין ממטתו בשעת תשמיש משום צניעות דאסור לשמש מטתו בפני כל חי. ל"א כליא עורב מונע העורבים כמו (תהילים מ׳:י״ב) לא תכלא רחמיך:
notes.en: A cubit, kalya orev: he mentions a cubit because we say in the last chapter of Menaḥot (107a): [One who says:] “Iron is upon me” may not give less than a cubit by a cubit, for the kalya orev. They would bring iron plates a cubit by a cubit, with tall spikes a cubit high fixed in them, and cover the top of the Sanctuary roof with them to drive away the ravens, so that they would not dwell there. Kalya means that it drives the ravens away, like the term in tractate Nidda (17a) for [a screen that] drives off flies, said of one who would drive the flies from his bed at the time of marital relations, for modesty, since relations are forbidden in the presence of any living creature. Another version: kalya orev, which holds back the ravens, as in “You will not withhold [tikhla] Your mercy” (Psalms 40:12).

notes.he: פי' הערוך זה לשונו לפי שבמקדש ראשון היתה קדושתו בכל הקהל והיתה שכינה שרויה בו ולא היו עופות פורחין עליו אבל במקדש שני פחדו מטעמא דאין קדושתו כקדושת ראשון שמא יפרחו העופות על המקדש וישליכו שם דבר טמא עשו צורה להבריח העופות מגג ההיכל וקראו אותו כליא עורב כלומר זאת מונעת העורבים מלפרוח בגג ההיכל וזו צורה כדרך שעושין עכשיו שומרי זרעים עד כאן לשונו ויש מקשה דאמר במועד קטן (דף ט.) גבי שלמה איבעי ליה לשיורי באמת כליא עורב ומשני אמת כליא עורב צורך בנין היא אלמא הוה בבית ראשון וי"ל שהיה שלמה ירא שמא לא תהא עליו קדושה וכשראו שהיה קדוש הסירוהו:
notes.en: Such as a cubit kalya orev: the Arukh explains, in these words: Since in the First Temple its sanctity was [felt] by the whole congregation, and the Divine Presence rested in it, birds would not fly over it. But in the Second Temple they feared, since its sanctity was not like the sanctity of the First, that birds might fly over the Sanctuary and drop something impure there. So they made a figure to scare the birds off the Sanctuary roof, and called it kalya orev, that is, this keeps the ravens from flying over the Sanctuary roof. It is a figure like those that crop-watchers make now. End of his words. Some object: it says in Mo’ed Katan (9a), regarding Solomon, that he should have left out the cubit of the kalya orev, and it answers that the cubit kalya orev is a need of the building; evidently it existed in the First Temple. One can say that Solomon feared that perhaps [the Temple] would not have sanctity, and when they saw that it was holy, they removed it.

messages.text: Nehemiah requested from the king of Persia: “And a letter to Asaph the keeper of the king’s park, that he may give me timber to make beams for the gates of the castle that pertains to the house.” Here Nehemiah clearly asked for material from gentiles.
messages.lead: Rav Yosef raises an objection to the ruling of the baraita as interpreted by Rabbi Yoḥanan, that with regard to the beginning of the building of the Temple nothing is accepted from gentiles.
messages.quote: With regard to the beginning of the building of the Temple, one may not accept even water and salt from them

verse.he: וְאִגֶּרֶת אֶל־אָסָף שֹׁמֵר הַפַּרְדֵּס אֲשֶׁר לַמֶּלֶךְ אֲשֶׁר יִתֶּן־לִי עֵצִים לְקָרוֹת אֶת־שַׁעֲרֵי הַבִּירָה אֲשֶׁר־לַבַּיִת וּלְחוֹמַת הָעִיר וְלַבַּיִת אֲשֶׁר־אָבוֹא אֵלָיו וַיִּתֶּן־לִי הַמֶּלֶךְ כְּיַד־אֱלֹהַי הַטּוֹבָה עָלָי׃
verse.en: likewise, a letter to Asaph, the keeper of the King’s Park, directing him to give me timber for roofing the gatehouses of the temple fortress and the city walls and for the house I shall occupy.” The king gave me these, thanks to my God’s benevolent care for me.

notes.dh: ואגרת אל אסף שומר הפרדס וגו'
notes.he: והיינו בתחילת בנין וקשקיל בדק הבית מכורש:
notes.en: “And a letter to Asaph the keeper of the king’s park,” etc.: this was at the beginning of the building, and he was taking [materials for] Temple maintenance from Cyrus.

notes.dh: מיתיבי ואגרת אל אסף שומר הפרדס
notes.he: והיינו בתחילת הבנין וקשקיל בדק הבית מכורש לשון קונטרס ולא נראה דהא כל הבנין משל כורש היה וכמה קראי איכא גם כתיב ומה חשחן אימריא וגו' ונ"ל דודאי מזה אינו מקפיד דהא היה בגזירה כך וביד ישעיה (ישעיהו מ״ה:י״ג) הוא יבנה עירי אבל אל אסף שומר הפרדס היה רחוק מכורש ולא היה שלו ממש אך היה גוזר שיתנו לצורך בדק הבית שהיה מוטל עליהם שהיה מולך בכיפה בהא איכא למיחש או לרפיון ידים או לערעור כדפרישית:
notes.en: They raised an objection: “And a letter to Asaph the keeper of the park”: “And this was at the beginning of the building, and he was taking Temple maintenance from Cyrus.” So says the Kuntres [Rashi]. This does not seem right, since the whole building was from Cyrus, and there are several verses [about it]; it is also written: “And that which they have need of, young bullocks, and rams, and lambs” (Ezra 6:9). It seems to me that certainly they were not particular about that, since it was by decree, and through Isaiah [it was said]: “He shall build My city” (Isaiah 45:13). But Asaph the keeper of the park was far from Cyrus and not truly his; rather, [the king] decreed that they give for the needs of Temple maintenance, which was imposed on them, since he ruled over the whole world. In this there is room for concern, either of weakening of hands or of contesting, as I explained.

notes.dh: אשר יתן לי עצים לקרות את שערי הבירה
notes.he: אלמא דמקבלין מהם דבר מסויים:
notes.en: That he may give me timber to make beams for the gates of the castle: evidently one accepts a defined item from them.

messages.text: @Rav Yosef Actions taken by the government are different, as the government does not retract its decisions.
messages.quote: And a letter to Asaph the keeper of the king’s park

notes.he: הואיל ותחילתו לטובה נתכוין שוב אינו חוזר:
notes.en: Does not retract: since at the outset it intended good, it does not go back on it afterward.

notes.he: מאחר דיהיבה לא חיישינן שיבקש שיחזירו' לו [דאמר שמואל וכו':
notes.en: The government is different, as it does not retract: once it has given, we do not fear that it will ask for it to be returned to it, as Shmuel says, etc.

messages.text: If the government says: I will uproot mountains, it will uproot mountains and not retract what it said.

§ With regard to a gentile who separated teruma from his pile of grain, one examines him to determine his intent. If he separated it with the intent that it be like the teruma of Jews, it should be given to a priest. If not, it requires interment, as we are concerned that perhaps his heart was directed toward Heaven, i.e., his intent was to consecrate it to the Temple and he did not want it to be given to a priest. Since there is uncertainty with regard to his intent, nothing can be done with that produce.

notes.he: של תבואת עצמו:
notes.en: His pile: of his own grain.

notes.he: שלמקום שתרומת ישראל הולכת תלך זו. ל"א שישראל אמר לי להפרישה וראשון שמעתי:
notes.en: If he said: I separated it with the intent of Jews: that it should go wherever the teruma of Jews goes. Another version: that a Jew told him to separate it. The first is what I heard.

notes.he: ואסורה בהנאה דחיישינן שמא בלבו לשמים לשם הקדש הילכך יגנז. ובזמן הזה עסקינן דהקדש אסור בהנאה כדתניא בכורות (דף נג.) אין מקדישים ואין מעריכין בזמן הזה ואם הקדיש בהמה תיעקר פירות כסות וכלים ירקבו:
notes.en: It requires interment: and it is forbidden for benefit, since we are concerned that perhaps in his heart it was for Heaven, for consecrated property; therefore it is to be interred. And we are dealing with the present time, when consecrated property is forbidden for benefit [with no way to redeem it], as it is taught in Bekhorot (53a): One does not consecrate and does not valuate in the present time; and if one consecrated an animal, it is hamstrung; produce, clothing and vessels are left to rot.

notes.he: משמע דעובד כוכבים איתיה בתרומה דנפשיה וכן משמע פרק שני דגיטין (דף כג:) והא דקאמר בזבחים פרק בית שמאי (זבחים דף מה.) דליתיה בתרומה דנפשיה לא קשיא דתנאי נינהו בפרק שני דקדושין (דף מא:) דתנן תרומת עובד כוכבים מדמעת וחייבין עליה חומש ור' שמעון פוטר:
notes.en: If he said: I separated it with the intent of Jews: This implies that a gentile is [subject to the law of] teruma for his own [produce], and so it is implied in the second chapter of Gittin (23b). And what is said in Zevaḥim, chapter Beit Shammai (45a), that he is not [subject to] teruma for his own, is no difficulty, since it is a dispute of tanna’im, [cited] in the second chapter of Kiddushin (41b), as we learned: The teruma of a gentile renders [ordinary produce] a mixture, and one is liable for the [added] fifth for it; and Rabbi Shimon exempts.

notes.he: של עצמו]:
notes.en: His pile: his own.

notes.he: שאני רוצה לעשו' ממנה מה שישרא' עושה תנתן לכהן:
notes.en: If he said: I separated it with the intent of Jews: I want it to be done with it as a Jew does; it is given to a priest.

notes.he: שמא לדעת כן הפרישה שתהא קדושה קדושת גבוה כגון שיקנו ממנו עולה שתהא כולה לגבוה ואין רצונו שיאכלה כהן:
notes.en: Perhaps his heart was toward Heaven: perhaps he separated it with this intent, that it should have the sanctity of the Most High, for example that a burnt offering be bought with it, which is entirely for the Most High, and he does not want a priest to eat it.

messages.text: The Gemara raises an objection from a baraita:

In the case of a gentile who donated a cross beam and brought it to a synagogue, and the name of God is written on it, one examines him to determine his intent. If he says: I separated it with the intent that it be like the donations of Jews, the name should be cut off [yagod] and interred, and one uses the remainder for a synagogue.

notes.he: יחתוך מקום השם ויגנוז החתיכה וישתמש במותר ויבננו בבית הכנסת:
notes.en: Yagod: he cuts off the place of the name and inters that piece, and uses the remainder, building it into the synagogue.

notes.he: משמע ע"י שיחתוך הקורה ולא יהנה מאותה חתיכה שכנגד השם דבמקומו מיהא קידש השם ויש ליזהר כשכותבין ס"ת או תפילין וגררו מקום השם שאין לכתוב במקומו:
notes.en: He cuts it off and uses the remainder: This implies [that he may use the rest] by cutting the beam, and not benefit from that piece opposite the name, since in its own place, at least, the name sanctified [the wood]. And one must be careful, when writing a Torah scroll or tefillin and scraping away the place of the name, not to write [something else] in its place.

notes.he: קודם לכן:
notes.en: And the [holy] name is written on it: beforehand.

notes.he: יקוץ [מן הקורה מקום השם וישתמש במותר לצורך ביהכ"נ:
notes.en: Yagur [so Rabbeinu Gershom’s text; the daf reads yagod]: he cuts off from the beam the place of the name, and uses the remainder for the needs of the synagogue.

messages.text: And if not, the entire beam requires interment, as we are concerned that perhaps his heart was directed toward Heaven, i.e., his intent was to consecrate it to the Temple, and therefore it may not be used.

notes.he: להקדש ובזמן הזה אין לו תקנה:
notes.en: For Heaven: for consecrated property; and in the present time it has no remedy.

notes.he: כדאמרן ולא שיהנה אדם ממנה:
notes.en: Perhaps his heart was toward Heaven: as we said, and not that a person should benefit from it.

messages.text: The reason that the beam requires interment is that the name of God is written on it, from which it may be inferred that if God’s name is not written on it, it does not require interment. Why, then, did Rav Yehuda say that if a gentile separated teruma it requires interment?
messages.quote: and the name of God is written on it

notes.he: דמוכחא מילתא דבלבו לשמים שהרי כתב עליה שמו של הקב"ה:
notes.en: The reason is that the name is written on it: for then the matter is evident that in his heart it was for Heaven, since he wrote the name of the Holy One, Blessed be He, on it.

messages.text: Even though the name of God is not written on the beam, the same halakha is true, and the beam requires interment, due to the concern that he might have intended to consecrate it.

And as for why the baraita specifically discusses the case where God’s name was written on the beam, this teaches us that if his intention was for it to be used in a synagogue, then even though God’s name is written on it, nevertheless the rest of the beam is not prohibited. Rather, the name should be cut off and interred, and one may use the remainder for a synagogue.

notes.he: כלומר משום רישא איצטרי' לאשמועי' דאית ביה רבותא]:
notes.en: And this teaches us: that is, it was needed to teach us [the case of the name] because of the first clause, since it contains a novelty.

messages.text: The reason is that if God’s name is written on an item, only the place where it is written is sanctified, but that part of the item that is not in its place is not sanctified.

notes.he: כלומר אינו קדוש אלא מקום השם ואותה חתיכה תיגנז והשאר יבנה בבית הכנסת כי אמר בדעת ישראל הפרשתיה. ל"א שם שלא במקומו כגון על גבי קורות וכלים לא קדיש דלא הוי מקומו אלא על הנייר ושיכתוב המקרא עם השם כנתינתו אבל שם לבדו הוי שלא במקומו ולא קדיש וראשון שמעתי והוא עיקר:
notes.en: A name not in its place is not sanctified: that is, only the place of the name is sanctified, and that piece is to be interred, while the rest is built into the synagogue, when he said: I separated it with the intent of Jews. Another version: a name not in its place, such as on beams and vessels, is not sanctified, since that is not its place; its place is only on parchment, with the verse written together with the name as it was given. But a name by itself is not in its place and is not sanctified. The first is what I heard, and it is the main one.

notes.he: [שלא במקום] הראוי לכתוב כגון בספר או במקום כבוד לא קדוש כדתנן כו':
notes.en: A name not in its place: not in the place fit to write it, such as in a book or a place of honor, is not sanctified, as we learned, etc.

messages.text: If one of the names of God was written on the handles of vessels or on legs of a bed, one must cut off the name and inter it, and the remainder is permitted.
One who says: I am contributing this sela to charity, is permitted to change its purpose, i.e., to use the money himself and later replace it.
messages.lead: § Rav Naḥman says that Rabba bar Abbahu says:

notes.he: לצרכיו ולאחר זמן ישלם:
notes.en: To change it: for his own needs, and after a time he will repay.

notes.he: ללוותה לצרכיו ולפורעה אחר זמן:
notes.en: It is permitted to change it: to borrow it for his needs and repay it after a time.

messages.text: It was initially understood from this that if one wants to change its purpose for his own benefit, yes, this is permitted, as he originally had this stipulation in mind. But it is not permitted to lend it to another. Yet it was stated:
messages.quote: is permitted to change its purpose

notes.he: להלוותה לחבירו לא דלעצמו איכא למימר על מנת כן היקצה לצדקה שאם יצטרך יטלנה וישלם אחרת אבל חבירו לא אסיק אדעתיה:
notes.en: But for another: to lend it to his fellow, no. For himself one can say that he set it aside for charity on this condition, that if he needed it he would take it and repay another [coin]; but [lending it to] his fellow did not occur to him.

notes.he: סבור מינה לעצמו מותר ללוותה דהוא אינו מאחרה שהרי הוא הקדישה אבל לאחר לא דלא איכפת ליה ומאחרה:
notes.en: It was understood from this: for himself it is permitted to borrow it, since he will not delay it, as he himself consecrated it; but for another, no, since [the other] does not care and will delay it.

messages.text: It is permitted to change its purpose whether for himself or for another.

They taught this halakha, that one may change the purpose of the coin, only in a case where he said: It is incumbent upon me to donate a sela to charity. But if he said: This sela is for charity, then he is required to give the sela to charity as is, and he may not use it and replace it.
messages.quote: this sela to charity, is permitted to change its purpose

notes.he: דמותר לשנותה אלא דאמר סלע זו עלי לצדקה דכיון דאמר עלי וקיבלה באחריות לענין גניבה ואבידה כדידיה דמי:
notes.en: They taught only: that he may change it, where he said: This sela is upon me for charity [Rashi’s wording joins “this” and “upon me”]. Since he said “upon me,” and accepted responsibility for it with regard to theft and loss, it is like his own.

notes.he: ולא אמר עלי בעינא בעי למיתב:
notes.en: But if he said: This is: and did not say “upon me,” he must give [it as is].

notes.he: לא שנו דמותר לשנותה אלא דאמר עלי דכיון דניתחייב באחריותה ודאי פורעה:
notes.en: They taught that it is permitted to change it only where he said “upon me”: since he became liable for responsibility for it, he will certainly repay it.

messages.text: On the contrary, the opposite is more reasonable. In a case where one said: This sela is for charity, it makes sense to allow him to use it, so that he should bear financial responsibility for its loss from that point onward. But if he said: It is incumbent upon me to donate a sela to charity, he should not be allowed to use the sela, as in any event he must donate a sela.
messages.quote: But if he said: This sela is for charity, then he is required to give the sela to charity as is

notes.he: דכיון דמשתמש הוי כשולח יד בפקדון וקמה לה ברשותיה לענין תשלומין אבל אמר עלי דבלאו הכי מיחייב באחריות לא ישתמש:
notes.en: So that he should bear responsibility for it: since by using it he is like one who misappropriates a deposit, and it comes into his possession with regard to payment. But [where he] said “upon me,” he is liable for it in any case, so he should not use it.

notes.he: דהיינו הנאת הקדש:
notes.en: So that he should bear responsibility for it: which amounts to benefit from consecrated property.

messages.text: Rather, as there is a reason in either situation to permit its use, there is no difference between the cases, and in both cases he may use the sela.

notes.he: ומותר:
notes.en: Rather, there is no difference: and it is permitted.

notes.he: דבין אמר עלי ובין אמר זו מותר לשנותה:
notes.en: Rather, there is no difference: whether he said “upon me” or said “this,” it is permitted to change it.

messages.text: It is taught in a baraita in accordance with the opinion of Rava:
A vow is charity, but consecrated property is not charity.
What is the baraita saying? After all, neither a vow nor consecrated property is charity.
messages.quote: A vow is charity, but consecrated property is not charity

notes.he: דסתם נדר דמי עלי לב"ה:
notes.en: Neither a vow is charity: since an unspecified vow is “The value of [this] is upon me for Temple maintenance.”

messages.text: Rather, is it not correct that this is what the baraita is saying: Charity is like a vow to consecrate property, in that it is subject to the prohibition of: You shall not delay, which is derived from the verse: “When you shall vow a vow to the Lord your God, you shall not delay to pay it.”

verse.he: כִּי־תִדֹּר נֶדֶר לַיהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לֹא תְאַחֵר לְשַׁלְּמוֹ כִּי־דָרֹשׁ יִדְרְשֶׁנּוּ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ מֵעִמָּךְ וְהָיָה בְךָ חֵטְא׃
verse.en: When you make a vow to the ETERNAL your God, do not put off fulfilling it, for the ETERNAL your God will require it of you, and you will have incurred guilt;

notes.he: והכי משמע נדר הוא הצדקה דקאי עליה בבל תאחר כנדר דקאמר בפרק קמא דר"ה (דף ו.) בפיך זו צדקה:
notes.en: Under “You shall not delay”: and this is the meaning: charity is a vow, in that it stands under “You shall not delay,” like a vow, as is said in the first chapter of Rosh HaShana (6a): “With your mouth” (Deuteronomy 23:24): this is charity.

notes.he: צדקה הוי כנדר לעבור עליה בבל תאחר:
notes.en: Charity is like a vow, so that one transgresses “You shall not delay” with regard to it.

messages.text: But nevertheless it is not like consecrated property, as in the case of consecrated property it is prohibited to use it, while in the case of charity it is permitted to use it. Since with regard to the option of using the money the baraita does not distinguish between a case where one says: It is incumbent upon me to donate a sela to charity, and a case where he says: This sela is for charity, it evidently supports the opinion of Rava.

notes.he: משמע ליה דאיירי בין זו בין עלי וכן הפסק כרב נחמן האומר סלע זו לצדקה מותר לשנותה בין לעצמו בין לאחר בין אמר עלי בין אמר זו ולשנותה היינו ללותה:
notes.en: While charity, it is permitted to use it: He understands that it deals with both “this” and “upon me.” And so the ruling is like Rav Naḥman: one who says: This sela is for charity, may change it, whether for himself or for another, whether he said “upon me” or “this.” And “to change it” means to borrow it.

messages.text: I said this halakha of Rav Naḥman’s, with regard to one who says: This sela is for charity, along with the accompanying discussion, before Rav Zevid from Neharde’a.
messages.quote: One who says: I am contributing this sela to charity, is permitted to change its purpose

notes.he: דהאומר סלע זו לצדקה כו':
notes.en: This halakha: that of one who says: This sela is for charity, etc.

messages.text: @Rav Kahana You teach this halakha in this manner, that Rav Naḥman merely stated that it is permitted to change the purpose of the sela, and the Sages clarified that it is permitted in all cases. But we teach this halakha in this manner, that it was all stated citing Rav Naḥman:

notes.he: דרב נחמן מותר לשנותה סתמא קאמר ורבי אמי פירשה בין לעצמו בין לאחר ורבא הדר פירשה בין עלי בין הרי זו אנן בהדיא מתנינן כו' ופירושה כדרב נחמן:
notes.en: You teach it this way: that Rav Naḥman said “it is permitted to change it” without specification, and Rabbi [Davidson: Rav] Ami explained it as whether for himself or for another, and Rava then explained it as whether [he said] “upon me” or “this is.” We teach it explicitly, etc., and the whole explanation is in the words of Rav Naḥman.

messages.alt: in Rav Zevid’s version, citing Rav
messages.text: One who said: I am contributing this sela to charity, is permitted to change its purpose, whether for himself or for another, and whether he said: It is incumbent upon me, or whether he said: This sela is for charity.

One who said: This sela is for charity, is permitted to change its purpose and replace it, as long as it has not yet come into the possession of the charity collectors. But once it has come into the possession of the charity collectors it is prohibited to change its purpose.
messages.lead: § The Sages taught a baraita which further deals with these matters:

notes.dh: עד שלא באתה ליד גבאי מותר לשנותה
notes.he: רבינו ברוך פירש מותר לשנותה ממש למצוה אחרת ואם נדר אדם סלע לצדקה לעניים יכול לעשות ממנו מצוה אחרת כל כמה דלא אתאי ליד גבאי אבל לישנא לשנותה לא משמע כן כך מצאתי כתוב בתוספות הר"ר משה מאוירא מכתיבת אחיו ופירש לא משמע לשנותה למצוה אחרת דלעיל קאמר מותר לשנותה בין הוא בין אחר היינו ללוותה ותו מדאמר והא רבי ינאי יזיף משמע דללוותה קאמר הילכך נראה לומר דללוותה קאמר אבל לשנותה ודאי אסור כי נמי לא באתה ליד גבאי אבל ללוותה קאמר ומשבאת ליד גבאי אסור ללוותה והא דקאמר פ"ק דב"ב (דף ח:) רשאין בני העיר לעשות קופה תמחוי היינו ברשות בני העיר אבל גבאי עצמו אסור ואומר ר"י דהתם רשאין לשנותה שלא לדבר מצוה רק שיהא צרכי צבור ויש ליזהר מללוות מעות צדקה העיר משבאתה ליד גבאי ואפי' ברשות הקהל נמי כיון שאין זה צורכי צבור. כך מצאתי כתוב:
notes.en: As long as it has not come into the possession of the charity collector, it is permitted to change it: Rabbeinu Barukh explained “permitted to change it” literally, [to use it] for another mitzva: if a person vowed a sela as charity for the poor, he may do another mitzva with it as long as it has not reached the collector. But the expression “to change it” does not imply this. So I found written in the Tosafot of Rabbi Moshe of Évreux, from the writing of his brother; and he explained that “to change it” does not mean for another mitzva, since above it says “permitted to change it, whether for himself or for another,” which means to borrow it. Moreover, from what is said, “But Rabbi Yannai borrowed,” it implies that it is speaking of borrowing. Therefore it seems one should say that it is speaking of borrowing; but to change it [to another purpose] is certainly forbidden even when it has not come into the collector’s possession. It speaks of borrowing, and once it has come into the collector’s possession, it is forbidden to borrow it. And what is said in the first chapter of Bava Batra (8b), “The townspeople may turn the [charity] fund into the soup kitchen,” is with the permission of the townspeople, but the collector himself is forbidden. And the Ri says that there they may change it even not for a matter of mitzva, as long as it is for communal needs. And one must be careful not to borrow the town’s charity money once it has reached the collector, even with the permission of the community, since this is not a communal need. So I found written.

notes.he: ודוקא יחיד אבל בני העיר רשאין כדמשמע בבבא בתרא (דף ח:) ורשאין בני עיר לעשות תמחוי קופה וקופה תמחוי ולשנותה לכל מה שירצו ודוקא לדבר מצוה כדאמרינן בשילהי שמעתא (ע"ב) גבי ישראל שהתנדב מנורה או נר לבית הכנסת והא דאמר בהשוכר האומנין (ב"מ דף עח:) מגבת פורים לפורים ומגבת אותה העיר לאותה העיר דוקא ומחוץ לעיר אסור לשנותה (אבל לצורכי העיר מותרין) בגבאי מיירי ובהאי טעמא יש ליישב דאמרי' בריש שור שנגח (ב"ק דף לו:) (חנן בישא) [ההוא גברא] דתקע (לההוא גברא) [לחבריה דא"ל] הב ליה פלגא דזוזא אמר הואיל ופלגא דזוזא הוא לא בעינא ניתביה לעניים הדר אמר איזיל ואברי ביה נפשאי אמר [ליה] רב יוסף כבר זכו בה עניים ויש לתמוה היאך היה יכול לחזור בו אפי לא זכו בה עניים והאמרן בפ"ק דר"ה (דף ו.) בפיך זו צדקה אלא י"ל שהיה רוצה ללוותה ולשנותה ולפורעה לאחר זמן וקא"ל רב יוסף שבאת לידו והוא גבאי ואסור לשנותה א"נ י"ל שהיה סבור דאפי' צדקה ליתא הואיל ולא תפסי בה וקמ"ל רב יוסף דזכו בה עניים כמו מעמד שלשתם:
notes.en: In brief: The prohibition once it reaches the collector applies only to an individual; the townspeople may change it, as Bava Batra (8b) implies: the townspeople may turn the fund into the soup kitchen and the soup kitchen into the fund, and change it for whatever they wish, but only for a matter of mitzva, as is said at the end of this passage (6b) about a Jew who donated a candelabrum or a lamp to a synagogue. What is said in Bava Metzia (78b), that a Purim collection is for Purim and a town’s collection is for that town, and outside the town it is forbidden to change it, speaks of the collector. By this reasoning Tosafot settles Bava Kamma (36b): a man who struck his fellow was told to give him half a zuz; [the victim] said, since it is only half a zuz I don’t want it, let it go to the poor; then he said, I will go and restore myself with it; and Rav Yosef told him the poor had already acquired it. Tosafot asks how he could have retracted even had the poor not acquired it, since Rosh HaShana (6a) says “With your mouth: this is charity.” Answer: he wanted to borrow it and repay later, and Rav Yosef told him that since it had come into his hand and he was [as] the collector, it was forbidden to change it. Alternatively, he thought it was not charity at all since [the poor] had not taken hold of it, and Rav Yosef taught that the poor acquired it, as in a transfer made in the presence of all three. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

messages.caption: “This sela is for charity”: may he use it and repay? The opinions of 6a, and the limit set by the baraita.

messages.text: 6b
Is that so? But Rabbi Yannai, who was a charity collector, borrowed money belonging to charity and repaid.
messages.quote: once it has come into the possession of the charity collectors it is prohibited to change its purpose

notes.he: גבאי הוה ויזיף מעות הצדקה לצורכו ופרע:
notes.en: Rabbi Yannai: was a charity collector, and he borrowed the charity money for his own needs and repaid.

notes.he: דהוה גבאי יזיף לעצמו ופרע אע"ג דבאתה לידו:
notes.en: But Rabbi Yannai: who was a collector, borrowed for himself and repaid, even though it had come into his hand.

messages.text: The case of Rabbi Yannai is different; it is beneficial to the poor that he be allowed to borrow and repay, as the longer he leaves the charity fund empty, the more he impels people to give charity, and he thereby brings more money to the poor.
messages.quote: But Rabbi Yannai, who was a charity collector, borrowed money belonging to charity and repaid

notes.he: רבי ינאי דלית ליה זוזי למפרע ניחא להו לעניים:
notes.en: As the longer he leaves it: as long as Rabbi Yannai has no money to repay, it is good for the poor.

notes.he: רבי ינאי לציבורא ואמר דלית ליה מעות לחלק לעניים וכופה אותם לצדקה ואיכא רווחא לעניים:
notes.en: He impels: Rabbi Yannai [impels] the public, saying that he has no money to distribute to the poor, and presses them to [give] charity, and the poor gain.

notes.he: שאינו יכול לפורעה ואין בכיס צדקה מעשה לרבים דלית בו צדקה ומייתי להו לעניים יותר ממה שהוא חייב לכיס והוי הנאה לעניים ולבסו' דאית גביה היה פורעה אבל איניש אחרינא אסור לשנותה מאחר שבאתה ליד גבאי:
notes.en: As the longer he leaves it: since he cannot repay it, and there is nothing in the charity purse, he impels the public, [telling them] there is no charity in it, and he brings the poor more than he owes the purse; it is a benefit for the poor, and in the end, when he had [the money], he would repay it. But anyone else is forbidden to change it once it has come into the collector’s hand.

messages.text: In the case of a Jew who donated a candelabrum or a lamp to the synagogue, it is prohibited to change it and use it for another purpose.
messages.lead: The Sages taught a baraita that deals with a similar matter:

notes.he: כמשמעה:
notes.en: A candelabrum: as it sounds.

notes.he: קרוישוי"ל של כסף או של זהב:
notes.en: A lamp: (Rashi adds an Old French gloss) of silver or of gold.

notes.he: פמוט:
notes.en: A candelabrum: a candlestick.

messages.text: There is no difference whether he wishes to change it for a voluntary matter or for a matter involving a mitzva, as in both cases it is prohibited.
messages.lead: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba thought to say:
messages.quote: it is prohibited to change it

notes.he: אפי' לפדיון שבויים:
notes.en: No difference for a matter of mitzva: even for redeeming captives.

messages.text: @Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba This is what Rabbi Yoḥanan says: When the Sages taught the baraita, they taught only that it is prohibited when he changes it for a voluntary matter, but it is permitted to change it for a matter involving a mitzva.
messages.quote: There is no difference

messages.text: With regard to a gentile who donated a candelabrum or a lamp to the synagogue, if it is before its owner’s name has been forgotten, i.e., people still remember that he donated the item, it is prohibited to change it and use it for another purpose. Once its owner’s name has been forgotten, it is permitted to change it.
messages.lead: This halakha is derived from the fact that Rabbi Asi says that Rabbi Yoḥanan says:

notes.he: כלומר מדנקט ר' אסי עובד כוכבים דפעי וצועק למה שניתם ממה שנתתי מכלל דישראל דלא פעי שרי לשנויי לדבר מצוה דאי בישראל אסור ל"ל למנקט עובד כוכבים:
notes.en: From what Rabbi Asi says, etc.: that is, since Rabbi Asi mentioned a gentile, who cries out and screams: Why did you change what I gave? By implication, with a Jew, who does not cry out, it is permitted to change it for a matter of mitzva. For if with a Jew it were forbidden, why would he need to mention a gentile?

notes.he: ממנה שעדיין אומרים זו היא מנורה נדבתו של פלוני עובד כוכבים:
notes.en: Before its owner’s name has been forgotten: from it, since people still say: This is the candelabrum donated by so-and-so the gentile.

notes.he: דפעי:
notes.en: It is prohibited to change it: since he screams.

notes.he: עד שלא נשתקע שם בעליה אסור לשנותה (וטעמא דעובד כוכבים כי לא נשתקע בעליה) שאדם זוכר מי הקדישה ואומרין זו מנורה של פלוני:
notes.en: Before its owner’s name has been forgotten, it is prohibited to change it: (and the reason [applies to] a gentile, when [the name of] its owner has not been forgotten) since people remember who consecrated it and say: This is the candelabrum of so-and-so.

messages.text: With regard to what purpose is it stated that one may not change it before the owner’s name was forgotten? If we say that it is prohibited to change it for a voluntary matter, why does the baraita specifically mention a gentile? It is prohibited to change it in this manner even if it was donated by a Jew.
messages.quote: it is prohibited to change it

notes.he: קאמר ר' אסי דאסור לשנותה אילימא כו':
notes.en: With regard to what: does Rabbi Asi say that it is prohibited to change it? If we say, etc.

notes.dh: אילימא לדבר הרשות מאי איריא עובד כוכבים אפילו ישראל נמי
notes.he: הכי נמי מצי למימר מאי איריא לא נשתקע שם בעליה אפי' נשתקע נמי:
notes.en: If you say for a voluntary matter, why specifically a gentile? Even a Jew too: he could equally have said: why specifically before its owner’s name has been forgotten? Even once it has been forgotten too.

notes.he: כל זמן שלא נשתקע שם בעליה אסור לשנותה:
notes.en: Even a Jew too: as long as its owner’s name has not been forgotten, it is prohibited to change it.

messages.text: Rather, the baraita must be dealing with a change for a matter involving a mitzva, and therefore it is prohibited only if the donor is a gentile and his name has not yet been forgotten. And the reason for this halakha is that it is specifically a gentile who would protest and scream: Where is the candelabrum that I donated? But in the case of a Jew, who would not protest and scream if they used his donation for a different mitzva, one may well change it.

notes.he: כי לא נשתקע שמו ממנה דאסור לשנותה אפי' לדבר מצוה דעובד כוכבים מיפעא פעי כשאינו רואה אותה צועק ואומר היכן היא מנורה שהקדשתי:
notes.en: And the reason is a gentile: as long as his name has not been forgotten from it, it is prohibited to change it even for a matter of mitzva, since a gentile screams: when he does not see it, he cries out and says: Where is the candelabrum that I consecrated?

messages.text: Sha’azrak, an Arab [tayya’a] merchant, donated a candelabrum to Rav Yehuda’s synagogue. Raḥava changed its purpose before Sha’azrak’s name was forgotten as the donor, and Rava became angry at Raḥava for not waiting.

notes.he: עובד כוכבים היה:
notes.en: Sha’azrak: was a gentile.

notes.he: שנייה רחבה. לדבר מצוה קודם דנשתקע ממנה שמו:
notes.en: [Sha’azrak the Arab: a gentile merchant.] Raḥava changed it: for a matter of mitzva, before his name had been forgotten from it.

messages.text: Some say the opposite: Rava changed its purpose, and Raḥava became angry at Rava.
And some say that the attendants of Pumbedita, the charity collectors, changed its purpose, and Raḥava became angry at them, and Rabba became angry at them as well.
The one who changed its purpose holds that it was permitted to change it, as it was not common for Sha’azrak to be in the city and it was unlikely that he would protest the change.

notes.he: שעזרק במתא דליפעי שסוחר היה ומחזר בעיירות:
notes.en: Not common: for Sha’azrak to be in town to scream, since he was a merchant who traveled around the towns.

notes.he: דהא לא שכיח שהולך תדיר לסחורתו ולא חזי לה ולא פעי ודמי כמי שנשתקע שמו ממנה:
notes.en: As it was not common: since he was always away on his trading, and would not see it and would not scream; so it is like a case where his name has been forgotten from it.

messages.text: And the one who became angry holds that even so, they should not have changed it, as sometimes he happens to come there.

notes.he: ולא חזי ליה ופעי:
notes.en: Sometimes he happens to come: and does not see it, and screams.

messages.text: Mishna
One who is moribund and one who is taken to be executed after being sentenced by the court is neither the object of a vow nor valuated.

notes.he: מפרש בגמרא טעמא:
notes.en: MISHNA: One who is moribund and one who is taken to be executed, etc.: the Gemara explains the reason.

messages.text: He is not the object of a vow, because he has no market value; but he is valuated, due to the fact that one’s value is fixed by the Torah based on age and sex.

notes.he: איוצא ליהרג פליג אבל בגוסס מודה דכתיב (ויקרא כ״ז:ח׳) והעמיד והעריך אותו וגוסס לאו בר העמדה והערכה הוא:
notes.en: Rabbi Ḥanina ben Akavya: disagrees about one taken to be executed, but about the moribund he agrees, since it is written: “Then he shall be set… and [the priest] shall value him” (Leviticus 27:8), and one who is moribund is not subject to setting and valuation.

notes.he: בפרשה ערכין אבל אנודר מודה דהא כנמכר בשוק בעי למשיימיה וזה אינו נמכר בשוק כלומר שאין אדם קונהו ויפסיד מעותיו:
notes.en: That one’s value is fixed: in the passage of valuations. But about [being the object of] a vow he agrees [that he is not vowed], since [then] one must assess him as [a slave] sold in the market, and this one is not sold in the market, that is, no one would buy him and lose his money.

messages.text: One with that status vows to donate the assessment of another person to the Temple treasury, and takes vows of valuation, and consecrates his property; and if he damages the property of others, he is liable to pay compensation.

notes.he: ובגמרא מפרש מאי קא אתי ר' יוסי למימר הא ת"ק לא אמר אינו נודר שאם אמר דמי פלוני עלי יפטר דהא לא נידר קאמר:
notes.en: He vows and valuates, etc.: the Gemara explains what Rabbi Yosei comes to say, since the first tanna did not say “he does not vow,” such that if he said: The value of so-and-so is upon me, he would be exempt; he said only “he is not vowed.”

messages.text: Gemara

Granted, it makes sense that one who is moribund is not the object of a vow, as he has no monetary value. And it also stands to reason that he is not valuated, as he is not subject to setting, i.e., standing, and therefore is not subject to valuation. The verse states: “Then he shall be set before the priest, and the priest shall value him.” This teaches that anyone who cannot stand, such as one who is dying, is not included in the halakha of valuation.
messages.quote: One who is moribund and one who is taken to be executed is neither the object of a vow nor valuated

verse.he: וְאִם־מָךְ הוּא מֵעֶרְכֶּךָ וְהֶעֱמִידוֹ לִפְנֵי הַכֹּהֵן וְהֶעֱרִיךְ אֹתוֹ הַכֹּהֵן עַל־פִּי אֲשֶׁר תַּשִּׂיג יַד הַנֹּדֵר יַעֲרִיכֶנּוּ הַכֹּהֵן׃ {ס}
verse.en: But if someone cannot afford the equivalent, they shall be presented before the priest, and the priest shall make an assessment; the priest shall make the assessment according to what the vower can afford.

notes.he: שאינו יכול לעמוד שהוא כמת וכתיב והעמיד והעריך]:
notes.en: Since he is not subject to setting and valuation: he cannot stand, since he is like a dead man, and it is written: “And he shall set… and he shall value.”

messages.text: But with regard to one who is taken to be executed, granted, he is not the object of a vow, as he has no monetary value, since no one would purchase him. But with regard to the mishna’s statement that he is not valuated, why not?

notes.dh: גמ' אלא לא נערך אמאי לא
notes.he: הרי דמיו קצובין:
notes.en: GEMARA: But why is he not valuated? His value is fixed.

messages.text: The reason is as it is taught in a baraita:

From where is it derived that in the case of one who is being taken to be executed and who said: My valuation is upon me to donate to the Temple, that he did not say anything, and the valuation is not collected from his estate? The verse states: “Anything dedicated [ḥerem], that may be dedicated of men, shall not be redeemed.”

verse.he: כׇּל־חֵרֶם אֲשֶׁר יׇחֳרַם מִן־הָאָדָם לֹא יִפָּדֶה מוֹת יוּמָת׃
verse.en: No human being who has been proscribed can be ransomed: they shall be put to death.

notes.dh: מנין ליוצא ליהרג ואמר ערכי עלי שלא אמר כלום
notes.he: ומשום דליתא בדמים ליכא למעוטי דהא איתרבו לעיל (ערכין דף ב.) מנוול ומוכה שחין:
notes.en: From where [is it derived] that one taken to be executed who said: My valuation is upon me, did not say anything: And it cannot be excluded [merely] because he has no monetary value, for above (Arakhin 2a) the repulsive and one afflicted with boils were included [in valuations].

notes.he: כלומר כל העומד ליהרג לא יפדה ערכו שאינו נערך:
notes.en: Anything dedicated shall not be redeemed: that is, anyone who stands to be executed, his valuation is not redeemed, since he is not valuated.

messages.text: This teaches that with regard to one who is worthy of excommunication [ḥerem], i.e., condemned to death, one cannot redeem him, i.e., pay his valuation. One might have thought that this applies even before his verdict is issued, i.e., that this halakha applies even if one issued this statement before being sentenced to death. Therefore, the verse states: “Of men,” and not all men, i.e., only some men destined to be executed have no valuation, and not all of them.

notes.he: מי שהוא ראוי ליחרם וליהרג אינו בכלל פדיון:
notes.en: Anything dedicated shall not be redeemed: one who is fit to be dedicated [ḥerem] and executed is not included in redemption.

messages.text: And with regard to Rabbi Ḥanina ben Akavya, who says in the mishna that even a person taken to be executed is valuated, due to the fact that one’s value is fixed, what does he do with the phrase “anything dedicated”?
messages.quote: he is valuated, due to the fact that one’s value is fixed

notes.he: אפי' לאחר גמר דין:
notes.en: And according to Rabbi Ḥanina, who said he is valuated: even after the verdict.

notes.he: בתורה לפי שנים שיש לו:
notes.en: Due to the fact that one’s value is fixed: in the Torah, according to the years he has.

messages.text: He requires it for that which is taught in a baraita:

Since we found with regard to those executed at the hand of Heaven that they give money and their sins are atoned, as it is stated in the case of the owner of a forewarned ox that killed a person: “The ox shall be stoned, and its owner shall also be put to death. If there be laid upon him a ransom, then he shall give for the redemption of his life whatsoever is laid upon him,” one might have thought that even with regard to those liable to receive the death penalty at the hands of man it is so, that one can pay in lieu of execution. Therefore, the verse states: “Anything dedicated that may be dedicated of men, shall not be redeemed.”

verse.he: וְאִם שׁוֹר נַגָּח הוּא מִתְּמֹל שִׁלְשֹׁם וְהוּעַד בִּבְעָלָיו וְלֹא יִשְׁמְרֶנּוּ וְהֵמִית אִישׁ אוֹ אִשָּׁה הַשּׁוֹר יִסָּקֵל וְגַם־בְּעָלָיו יוּמָת׃ אִם־כֹּפֶר יוּשַׁת עָלָיו וְנָתַן פִּדְיֹן נַפְשׁוֹ כְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר־יוּשַׁת עָלָיו׃
verse.en: If, however, that ox has been in the habit of goring, and its owner, though warned, has failed to guard it, and it kills a man or a woman—the ox shall be stoned and its owner, too, shall be put to death. If ransom is imposed to redeem [the owner’s] life, whatever is imposed must be paid.

notes.he: כגון האי דכתיב השור יסקל וגם בעליו יומת והך מיתה ליכא למימר בידי אדם דהא אמרי' בפ"ק דסנהדרין (דף טו:) מות יומת המכה רוצח הוא על רציחתו אתה הורגו ואי אתה הורגו על רציחת שורו:
notes.en: For those executed at the hand of Heaven: such as what is written: “The ox shall be stoned, and its owner shall also be put to death.” And one cannot say that this death is at the hands of man, since we say in the first chapter of Sanhedrin (15b): “He that struck him shall surely be put to death; he is a murderer” (Numbers 35:21): for his own murder you execute him, but you do not execute him for the killing done by his ox.

notes.he: שנאמר השור יסקל וגם בעליו יומת מיתה בידי שמים וסמיך ליה אם כופר יושת עליו אלמא אית להו פדיון למומתים בידי שמים:
notes.en: That they give money and are atoned: as it is stated: “The ox shall be stoned, and its owner shall also be put to death,” a death at the hand of Heaven, and right after it: “If there be laid upon him a ransom.” Evidently those executed at the hand of Heaven have redemption.

messages.text: I have derived only that one cannot give payment in lieu of execution with regard to severe prohibitions punishable by the death penalty, e.g., blasphemy or cursing one’s father, for which no atonement is designated in the Torah for their unwitting violation.

notes.he: כגון מגדף ומקלל אביו דאם עשה בשוגג אינו בקרבן ולא בגלות:
notes.en: Whose unwitting violation is not designated for atonement: such as the blasphemer and one who curses his father, for if he did it unwittingly, there is neither an offering nor exile.

notes.he: מי שעומד לחרם ליהרג אין לו פדיון. מיתות חמורות שלא ניתנה שגגתן לכפרה כמו מגדף ומכה אביו ואמו:
notes.en: The verse states: “Anything dedicated shall not be redeemed”: one who stands to be dedicated, to be executed, has no redemption. Severe deaths, whose unwitting violation is not designated for atonement: such as the blasphemer and one who strikes his father or his mother.

messages.text: From where is it derived that the same applies to less severe prohibitions punishable by the death penalty, e.g., violating Shabbat or killing, for which atonement of an offering or exile is designated in the Torah for their unwitting violation? The verse states: “Anything dedicated,” to include all prohibitions punishable by court-administered execution.

notes.he: כלומר דקלות להך מילתא שניתנה שגגתן לכפרה כגון רוצח דשגגתו גולה ועובד ע"ז ומחלל שבת ובא על הערוה דשגגתו חטאת:
notes.en: Lesser deaths: that is, lesser for this matter, in that their unwitting violation is designated for atonement, such as a murderer, whose unwitting [killing brings] exile, and an idol worshipper, one who desecrates Shabbat, and one who engages in forbidden relations, whose unwitting [act brings] a sin offering.

notes.he: כל שאר חייבי מיתות ב"ד] ת"ל כל חרם. מרבה הני והני:
notes.en: Lesser deaths, whose unwitting violation is designated for atonement: all the other capital offenses of the court. The verse states: “Anything dedicated,” to include both these and those.

messages.text: § The mishna teaches, with regard to one who is taken to be executed, that Rabbi Yosei says: Such a person vows to donate the assessment of another person to the Temple treasury, and takes vows of valuation, and consecrates his property; and if he damages the property of others, he is liable to pay compensation.
messages.quote: vows to donate the assessment of another person to the Temple treasury, and takes vows of valuation

messages.text: And does the first tanna say that such a person does not vow to donate the assessment of another person to the Temple treasury and take vows of valuation, such that Rabbi Yosei could be understood as disputing his opinion? The first tanna merely said that such an individual is not subject to vows and valuations. What is the difference between their opinions?

notes.he: מי קאמר דאינו נודר מעריך ומקדיש:
notes.en: And does the first tanna say not? Does he say that he does not vow, valuate and consecrate?

messages.text: Rather, with regard to whether or not one who is taken to be executed can vow to donate the assessment of another person to the Temple treasury, and take vows of valuation, and consecrate his property, everyone, including the first tanna, agrees that he can.

notes.he: דודאי נדרו נדר והקדישו הקדש ומעריך את אחרים דהא בר דעה הוא:
notes.en: Everyone agrees: certainly his vow is a vow and his consecration is consecration, and he valuates others, since he is a person of understanding.

messages.text: When they disagree, it is in a case where he causes damage. The first tanna holds that if he causes damage he is not liable for payment, and Rabbi Yosei holds that if he causes damage he is liable to pay compensation.

notes.he: ובאם הקדיש לא פליגי שמיד שהקדיש חל הקדש ולא דמיא למלוה אבל יש להקשות אמאי לא פליגי באם נדר והעריך וי"ל דנקט הזיק משום דקתני חיוב בתשלומין (משום) [אהזיק] משמע דאהזיק לחודיה פליגי ובנודר ומעריך שמא יחול מיד אבל גובה מן היורשין ונודר ומעריך איצטריך דס"ד הואיל ואינו נידר ונערך נודר ומעריך נמי אינו קמ"ל דנודר ומעריך ומקדיש כשאר בני אדם:
notes.en: When they disagree, it is where he caused damage: And where he consecrated they do not disagree, since as soon as he consecrated, the consecration takes effect, and it is not like a loan. But one can ask: why do they not disagree where he vowed or valuated? One can answer: he mentions “caused damage” because [the mishna] teaches “liable” [to payment] about causing damage, which implies that they disagree about causing damage alone; and with vowing and valuating, perhaps [the obligation] takes effect at once, and then [the Temple] collects from the heirs. And “he vows and valuates” was needed, since you might have thought that since he is not vowed and not valuated, he also does not vow or valuate; it teaches us that he vows, valuates and consecrates like other people.

notes.he: אלא בהני לא פליגי אלא באם הזיק פליגי]:
notes.en: Rather, about these they do not disagree; they disagree only where he caused damage.

messages.text: With regard to what principle do these tanna’im disagree, as it is an accepted principle that one who causes damage must pay?

They disagree as to whether the payment can be collected from his estate. This depends on the question of whether or not one who is owed money from a loan by oral agreement, i.e., a loan given without a document that places a lien on the land, can collect from the heirs.
messages.quote: With regard to what principle do these tanna’im disagree

notes.he: כגון זה שהזיק ולא עמד בדין על כך קודם למיתה: תשלומי נזק כתובין בתורה ומדאורייתא משעבד ליה בעל כרחיה:
notes.en: A loan by oral agreement: such as this one, who caused damage and did not stand trial for it before his death. [On Rava’s line:] Payment for damage is written in the Torah, and by Torah law [his property] is bound to it even against his will.

notes.he: ונזקין הן כמלוה (הכתובה) על פה דלא הוי כחוב גמור הכתוב בשטר:
notes.en: A loan by oral agreement: and damages are like a loan by oral agreement, which is not like a full debt written in a document.

messages.text: The first tanna holds that one who is owed money from a loan by oral agreement cannot collect from the heirs, and Rabbi Yosei holds that one who is owed money from a loan by oral agreement can collect from the heirs.

In fact, everyone agrees that one who is owed money from a loan by oral agreement cannot collect from the heirs; and here the tanna’im disagree with regard to the status of a loan that is written in the Torah, i.e., a financial obligation decreed by Torah law, such as paying damages.
messages.quote: a loan by oral agreement

notes.he: [מלוה הכתובה בתורה דנזק הכתוב בתורה:
notes.en: A loan written in the Torah: damage, which is written in the Torah.

messages.text: The first tanna holds that a loan that is written in the Torah is not considered as though it is written in a document, and may not be collected from the heirs. Rabbi Yosei holds that such a loan is considered as though it is written in a document, and therefore it may be collected from the heirs.

notes.he: וגובה מן היורשין]:
notes.en: Is like one written in a document: and he collects from the heirs.

messages.text: And there are those who teach the dispute between Rava and Rav Yosef with regard to this baraita:

notes.he: להא דרב יוסף ורבה:
notes.en: And there are those who teach it: this [dispute] of Rav Yosef and Rabba [Davidson: Rava].

notes.he: ואיכא דמתני להא דר' יוסף דאמר במלוה ע"פ גובה כו' אהא היוצא ליהרג:
notes.en: And there are those who teach it: this [statement] of Rav Yosef, who said a loan by oral agreement is collected, etc., with regard to this [baraita] of one taken to be executed.

messages.text: In the case of one who is taken to be executed after being sentenced by the court, if he injured another he is liable for payment. But if others injured him they are exempt, as they would be if they injured a dead person.

notes.he: דבר דעה הוא:
notes.en: He is liable: since he is a person of understanding.

notes.he: דאין לו דמים ועומד הוא ליחבל וכל הנך איכא ליהרג בדיני ישראל קאמר:
notes.en: They are exempt: since he has no value, and he stands to be injured [in any case]. And all these [cases] speak of one to be executed under the laws of Israel.

messages.text: Even if it was he who injured others, he is exempt, as he cannot be brought back to stand before the court for judgment, since he must be executed without delay.
messages.quote: if he injured another he is liable for payment

notes.he: שאין אתה יכול להחזירו לב"ד ולעמוד בדין על מה שחבל שאין מענין את דינו:
notes.en: To be brought back to stand before the court: you cannot bring him back to the court to stand trial for what he injured, since one does not delay his sentence.

notes.he: שהואיל ונגמר דינו ליהרג אין חוזרין ומביאין אותו לפני ב"ד בשביל שחבל לפי שאין מענין את דינו אלא לאחר שנגמר דינו ליהרג [לאלתר] יהרג משום צער בעלי חיים:
notes.en: He cannot be brought back to stand before the court: since his verdict to be executed has been concluded, one does not go back and bring him before the court because he injured, since one does not delay his sentence; rather, once his verdict to be executed is concluded, he is executed [at once], because of the suffering of a living being [so as not to prolong his anguish].

messages.text: Continues on 7a: the Gemara asks whether the first tanna then holds that the condemned man can be brought back to court, and Rav Yosef explains the baraita by the dispute over a loan by oral agreement.
